How people sign in (see docs/configuration.md), rendered to the
KRITIK_AUTH_* variables, which win over the configuration file's `auth`
block. Each is left out when empty; secrets come from existing Secrets.

user.title: user

clientId.description: Client ID of an OAuth App, or of a GitHub App, to sign in with GitHub.
clientId.title: clientId

name.title: name

roleMappingExpr.title: roleMappingExpr

clientId.description: OAuth client ID at the issuer.
clientId.title: clientId

name.description: Existing Secret holding the client secret.
name.title: name

name.description: The sign-in button's label; empty is "SSO".

roleMappingExpr.description: CEL expression giving a role, or a map of accounts to roles (KRITIK_AUTH_OIDC_ROLE_MAPPING_EXPR, docs/configuration.md).
roleMappingExpr.title: roleMappingExpr

rolesClaim.title: rolesClaim

scopes.description: Scopes to request; empty is openid, email and profile.

config.description:
The configuration file holds the whole configuration (ADR-0019,
ADR-0021): sign-in (`auth`), the GitHub `apps`, the instance's
`providers`, `embedding` and `egress`, the `defaults` every repository
gets, the `repositories` entries keyed `owner/*` or `owner/name`, and the
`accounts` with their limits and providers. Sign-in, one app, one
provider, the default models and review settings and the embedder also
have `KRITIK_*` environment variables, which win over the file; the
`auth` values above render some, and `extraEnv` can set the others. The
file is either inline as `file`, rendered into a chart-managed ConfigMap,
or an existing ConfigMap with a `config.yaml` key. Secret material never
goes in the file: it names environment variables, `{ env: NAME }`, which
`secretEnv` sets from existing Secrets. kritik reads the file at startup
(ADR-0022): the pods carry a
checksum of `file`, so a change to it rolls them, while a change to an
`existingConfigMap` needs a restart, for example by stakater's Reloader
through `deploymentAnnotations`. The leader applies it to the store.

diffRetention.description: How long a review keeps the diff it was made from, the context it read and the repository files it named, at least 24h (KRITIK_DIFF_RETENTION, Go duration). Empty is kritik's default, 720h.
diffRetention.title: diffRetention

existingConfigMap.description: Existing ConfigMap holding the file under the `config.yaml` key; takes precedence over `file`. A change to it takes a restart.
existingConfigMap.title: existingConfigMap

extraEnv.description: Extra raw env vars merged into the kritik serve container (advanced).
extraEnv.title: extraEnv

file.description: (optional) The configuration file, as YAML: the whole configuration, from `auth` and `apps` to `repositories` and `accounts`. Passed through verbatim, not tpl'd. See docs/configuration.md.
file.title: file

indexGrace.description: How long the index of a repository that stopped running is kept (KRITIK_INDEX_GRACE, Go duration). Empty is kritik's default, 720h.
indexGrace.title: indexGrace

indexWorkers.description: Index jobs one replica runs at once (KRITIK_INDEX_WORKERS), rate-limited apart from reviews.
indexWorkers.title: indexWorkers

logLevel.description: Log level: debug, info, warn or error.
logLevel.title: logLevel

onboardWindow.description: How many onboarding index jobs the leader keeps queued or running at once (KRITIK_ONBOARD_WINDOW). 0 is kritik's default, 4.
onboardWindow.title: onboardWindow

pollInterval.description: How often the leader lists each app's open pull requests, its backstop for missed webhooks (KRITIK_POLL_INTERVAL, Go duration); `0s` turns polling off. Empty is kritik's default, 10m.
pollInterval.title: pollInterval

pollLookback.description: How far back a first or long-idle poll looks (KRITIK_POLL_LOOKBACK, Go duration). Empty is kritik's default, 24h.
pollLookback.title: pollLookback

reviewWorkers.description: Review jobs one replica runs at once (KRITIK_REVIEW_WORKERS); follow-ups share the count. A review or index job holds at most one runner pod, so runner pods never exceed `replicas` × (reviewWorkers + indexWorkers).
reviewWorkers.title: reviewWorkers

transcriptRetention.description: How long a review's transcript is kept, at least 24h (KRITIK_TRANSCRIPT_RETENTION, Go duration). Empty is kritik's default, 720h.
transcriptRetention.title: transcriptRetention

config.title: config

database.description:
Three Postgres connection strings, each from its own Secret. The
application role must not own the tables (row-level security), the owner
role runs migrations and applies configuration on the leader, and the
runner role is handed to runner Jobs and can only write its own run. On
CloudNativePG, declare `app` and `runner` under `spec.managed.roles` and
use the bootstrap owner as `owner`; see the README.

existingSecret.description: (required) Secret holding the application role's connection URI.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

role.description: Name of the application role, asserted at startup (not superuser, no BYPASSRLS, owns nothing).
role.title: role

existingSecret.description: (required) Secret holding the owner role's connection URI, used only by the leader for migrations and configuration sync.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

existingSecret.description: (required) Secret holding the runner role's connection URI; referenced by runner Jobs, never read by kritik serve.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

role.description: Name of the runner role, granted only what runner Jobs need.
role.title: role

database.title: database

deploymentAnnotations.description: Annotations added to the Deployment (e.g. `reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true"`). Pod-level annotations go in `podAnnotations`.
deploymentAnnotations.title: deploymentAnnotations

port.description: Port of the gateway the kritik serve pods run, on the pods and its Service: the forward proxy runner Jobs are handed as `HTTPS_PROXY`, allowing only the hosts the configuration names (github.com once an app is configured, `egress.allowHosts`), so runner pods need no direct internet egress (ADR-0008), and the model and similar-code endpoints a runner calls with a per-run token, so no provider key enters a runner pod (ADR-0004, ADR-0026).
port.title: port

global.description: Global values are values that can be accessed from any chart or subchart by exactly the same name.
global.title: global

apiVersion.description: HTTPRoute apiVersion; empty defaults to gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1.
apiVersion.title: apiVersion

enabled.description: Expose web.url through a Gateway API HTTPRoute.
enabled.title: enabled

parentRefs.description: Gateways (and listeners) this route attaches to.
parentRefs.title: parentRefs

image.description:
Default values for kritik.

Most string, list and map values below are rendered through Helm's `tpl`, so
they may carry template expressions that resolve at install time, e.g.
  ingress.hosts[0].host: kritik.{{ .Values.global.domain }}
Plain numbers and booleans, and `config.file`, are passed through as they are.

digest.description: Pin the image by digest (sha256:…); when set, overrides the tag. The release pipeline fills it with the published image's digest.
digest.title: digest

tag.description: Overrides the image tag; defaults to the chart appVersion.
tag.title: tag

image.title: image

imagePullSecrets.description: Image pull secrets for private registries, for the kritik serve pods and, through the runner ServiceAccount, runner Jobs and the tool images they mount.
imagePullSecrets.title: imagePullSecrets

ingress.description:
One Ingress, or one Gateway API HTTPRoute, for `web.url`, to the public
Service, which serves the webhooks under `/hooks` and the dashboard. The
host and path come from `web.url`.

tls.description: Ingress TLS configuration, e.g. `[{hosts: [kritik.example.com], secretName: kritik-tls}]`.
tls.title: tls

ingress.title: ingress

livenessProbe.description: Liveness probe, on the metrics port.
livenessProbe.title: livenessProbe

enabled.description: Create a Prometheus Operator ServiceMonitor for the metrics Service (requires its CRDs).
enabled.title: enabled

nameOverride.description: Override the chart name used in resource names.
nameOverride.title: nameOverride

networkPolicy.description:
NetworkPolicies (off by default): one for the service pods (ingress to the
webhook and metrics ports; egress to DNS, the forges and models over the
egress ports, and Postgres) and one for runner pods (egress only: DNS, the
git remote over the egress ports, and Postgres). The Postgres port is
allowed to any peer because the database may live in another namespace.

allowDNS.description: Allow DNS egress (UDP/TCP 53); the Cilium flavor allows it to kube-dns alone.
allowDNS.title: allowDNS

egressPorts.description: TCP ports the service pods may egress to for forges and model endpoints. Runner pods reach the gateway alone.
egressPorts.title: egressPorts

type.description: Policy flavor for your CNI: "default" (networking.k8s.io/v1 NetworkPolicy), "cilium" (CiliumNetworkPolicy) or "calico" (projectcalico.org/v3 NetworkPolicy).
type.title: type

networkPolicy.title: networkPolicy

enabled.description: Create a PodDisruptionBudget when there is more than one replica.
enabled.title: enabled

maxUnavailable.description: Maximum pods that may be unavailable, as a count or percentage; takes precedence over `minAvailable` when set.
maxUnavailable.title: maxUnavailable

minAvailable.description: Minimum pods that must stay available, as a count or percentage. Used unless `maxUnavailable` is set.
minAvailable.title: minAvailable

priorityClassName.description: PriorityClass for the pods. Empty uses the cluster default.
priorityClassName.title: priorityClassName

create.description: Create the Role and RoleBinding kritik serve needs: Jobs in the release namespace, their pods and logs, and the Secrets it hands them. Nothing cluster-wide.
create.title: create

readinessProbe.description: Readiness probe, on the metrics port. A replica is ready once it has a database connection and its listeners are up.
readinessProbe.title: readinessProbe

replicas.description:
kritik runs as one Deployment of `kritik serve`: webhooks, the dashboard,
the job queues, runner Jobs, the gateway and, on the replica holding the
leader lock, the leader duties (ADR-0024). Runner pods are not part of
it: serve creates them as Jobs, one per review and index run.
Replicas of kritik serve. Every replica serves webhooks and the dashboard and works jobs; exactly one holds the leader lock at a time. Two keep one serving while a rollout replaces the other (ADR-0022 §2.3).
replicas.title: replicas

resources.description: Resource requests and limits of the kritik serve pods.
resources.title: resources

runner.description:
Runner Jobs: one pod per review or index run, created by kritik serve in the
release namespace from the same image, running as a service account with
no permissions and a database role that can only touch its own run. The
server's Role reaches every Secret in the release namespace, so install
kritik into a namespace of its own.

deadline.description: Deadline of a runner Job (KRITIK_RUNNER_DEADLINE, Go duration). Empty is kritik's default, 15m.
deadline.title: deadline

image.description: Image for runner Jobs; empty uses the chart's image. The release's `-tools` tag (e.g. `ghcr.io/home-operations/kritik:1.2.3-tools`) adds curl, fd, gh and rg for an agentic review's `agent.commands`.
image.title: image

resources.description: Resources for runner pods (KRITIK_RUNNER_RESOURCES), copied into the pod spec.
resources.title: resources

runtimeClassName.description: RuntimeClass for runner Jobs (e.g. `gvisor`, `kata`). Advised: a runner parses untrusted repository content and runs what the model asks; a sandboxed runtime keeps it from the node's kernel. Empty uses the cluster default.
runtimeClassName.title: runtimeClassName

create.description: Create the runner ServiceAccount: no permissions, no token mounted, and the chart's `imagePullSecrets` so runner Jobs can pull from a private registry.
create.title: create

name.description: Runner ServiceAccount name; generated from the release name if empty.
name.title: name

tools.description: Command-line tools a runner pod mounts from an image for the agent's run tool (KRITIK_RUNNER_TOOLS, ADR-0011), each a `name`, a digest-pinned `image`, the `path` of its binaries and the `commands` it provides. Needs Kubernetes 1.33 or newer, which mounts an image volume with a subPath; the chart refuses to render them on an older cluster.
tools.title: tools

ttl.description: How long a finished Job stays for kubectl before Kubernetes removes it (Go duration); the run row keeps everything the Job knew.
ttl.title: ttl

runner.title: runner

secretEnv.description:
The secrets the configuration file names (GitHub App private keys and
webhook secrets, model keys, sign-in secrets) and the `KRITIK_*` secret
variables (ADR-0022 §2.2). Each entry sets the variable `name` in the
kritik serve pods from `key` of the existing Secret `secretName`; kritik
drops it from its own environment once read. Runner pods never get them:
each is handed its own per-run credentials.
Environment variables set from existing Secrets, for the configuration file's `{ env: NAME }` references.
secretEnv.title: secretEnv

securityContext.description: Container securityContext (no privilege escalation, read-only root filesystem, drops ALL capabilities).
securityContext.title: securityContext

port.description: Public port: the webhooks (`POST /hooks/{app}`) and the dashboard (ADR-0024 §2.2).
port.title: port

type.description: Service type of the public Service.
type.title: type

automount.description: Automount the API token, which kritik serve needs to create runner Jobs.
automount.title: automount

create.description: Create the ServiceAccount kritik serve runs as.
create.title: create

name.description: ServiceAccount name; generated from the release name if empty.
name.title: name

startupProbe.description: Startup probe, on the metrics port. The liveness and readiness probes wait until it passes, so a pod still opening its listeners is not reported unready; it allows a minute.
startupProbe.title: startupProbe

strategy.description: Deployment update strategy. A rolling update that surges one pod and takes none down keeps one replica serving while the other is replaced (ADR-0022 §2.3). Helm merges maps, so a switch to `Recreate` also sets `rollingUpdate: null`.
strategy.title: strategy

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Grace period for a clean shutdown: kritik serve keeps accepting webhooks, dashboard requests and model steps for 5s while traffic moves off the pod, stops taking jobs and lets running ones finish for up to 100s, then retries the reviews it cut, and its gateway lets model steps in flight finish for up to 2m.
terminationGracePeriodSeconds.title: terminationGracePeriodSeconds

tests.description:
Config for the chart's `helm test` hook: a one-shot pod that curls the
metrics Service's /readyz to prove the release serves. Used only by `helm
test`, never the workload.

repository.description: `helm test` connection-pod image; a gcr-mirrored curl, so the test never pulls from Docker Hub.
repository.title: repository

tests.title: tests

topologySpreadConstraints.description: Spread the kritik serve pods across nodes, so a node loss does not take both replicas: a soft constraint, so a one-node cluster still schedules them. Rendered through `tpl`; empty leaves scheduling to Kubernetes.
topologySpreadConstraints.title: topologySpreadConstraints

volumeMounts.description: Additional volume mounts on the kritik serve container.
volumeMounts.title: volumeMounts

web.description:
The one public URL: the dashboard at `web.url`, and the webhooks under it
at `/hooks`, both served on `service.port`, which the Ingress or HTTPRoute
below route to.

url.description: (required) Public URL the dashboard is reached at, e.g. https://kritik.example.com; the webhooks share it under `/hooks/<app name>`. Must be an absolute http(s) URL with no query or fragment.
url.title: url

web.title: web
